newsitem.title: FRANCE: Zaire opposition leader to meet Mobutu in France.
newsitem.headline: Zaire opposition leader to meet Mobutu in France.

text.p: Zaire's radical opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi arrived in the south of France on Thursday for talks with Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko on the rebellion in eastern Zaire.

Tshisekedi, who said last week he was prepared to form a government to resolve the crisis, arrived at Nice airport from Paris on Thursday morning to meet Mobutu, convalescing in a private mansion on the Riviera after cancer surgery in August.

Mobutu, in power in Zaire for three decades, said in an interview with CNN that he had been stabbed in the back during his absence by "devils" invading the east of Zaire. "After my convalescence, I'll return to Zaire as president," he said.
Mobutu arrived in France from Switzerland on November 4 planning to stay for several weeks and has held a string of consulations on the crisis at his luxury villa at Roquebrune-Cap-Martin.

The U.N. said on Thursday it sent an assessment team into eastern Zaire's Bukavu to track down up to 700,000 missing Rwandan Hutu refugees central to a multinational debate over planned military intervention.

Tshisekedi is the principal figure in the opposition to Mobutu and still lays claim to the position of prime minister he held in 1992. Mobutu pushed him aside the following year and the two last met officially in December 1992.
Since arriving in France, Mobutu has also met U.N. envoy Raymond Chretien, Congo President Pascal Lissouba, Zairean Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo and Gabonese President Omar Bongo.
